verdict.rationale: Chime SDK docs state that meeting attendees can send each other real-time data messages alongside audio and video content, which supports custom features such as whiteboarding, chat, emoji reactions and floor-control signaling. This is a first-party, documented in-session data channel, though each message is capped at 2 KB. Missing for 10: API reference detail (method names, ordering and reliability semantics), latency figures, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, participants exchange low-latency arbitrary data in the session alongside audio and video, with a documented data API

citations.quote: In addition to audio and video content, meeting attendees can send each other real-time data messages of up to 2 KB each.
You can use messages to implement custom meeting features such as whiteboarding, chat, real-time emoji reactions, and application-specific floor control signaling.
